en: There also is one other
feature you should know about when working
with PySessions.
As they get longer, you may run out of space
in your context window. Obviously not a case
here.
And we also saw that we can use tree to
manage that. And that is indeed a very
efficient approach, which I personally like
a lot.
But let's say you're in your session and
you're slowly but steadily running out of
space and you need to
There is a command for that, and that is
/compact, which performs something called
compaction, which means it summarizes the
session. It's not the same as the tree
summary though. I mean, kind of it is. It
creates a summary with help of AI, but
unlike tree, it does not move you to a
different point in the session. Instead, you
stay where you are. It just throws away all
the old context and replaces it with a
summary.
So like tree, kind of, but not in a new
branch.
So if I run compact, it starts compacting.
You can cancel, of course.
If you run
/compact with a custom prompt,
so something like summarize key changes,
include list of files touched,
that will also create a summary, but based
on a custom prompt.
Either way, a summary will be created. Old
context will be thrown away and will be
replaced with that summary, but still in the
same branch, which is what makes tree more
powerful because it allows you to navigate
branches and create new branches instead of
working in one single branch, which you
reset over and over again.
You can do that, but tree gives you more
flexibility. And it's also worth noting that
this compaction will also happen
automatically if you come close to 100%.
So you don't even need to run it on your
own, but you might wanna do that, especially
if you want a custom prompt, if you know
that you're already
getting close to the context window limit.
But technically you don't have to.
Compaction will happen automatically if you
run out of space, but for more control, you
can do it manually.
Either way, I personally prefer tree for the
added flexibility and for having these
different branches. But of course, you see,
that's the summary. You can also use compact
instead.
But now if I were to use tree, you see it's
just another entry in the existing branch,
in the existing session here. It did not
create a new branch, which is the important
difference to tree as mentioned. Still
compact, also an important command to know
and an important concept in general to be
aware of.
